## Install the catchment package

The `catchment` package is on GitHub, not CRAN. This chunk installs it only if it is missing, so it is quick once the package is installed.

```{r}
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
if (!requireNamespace("catchment", quietly = TRUE)) remotes::install_github("uva-bi-sdad/catchment")
```

## Load the packages

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, tmap, catchment, tidyverse)
```

## Import the data

```{r}
mpsz <- st_read(dsn = "data/chap17/geospatial", layer = "MP14_SUBZONE_NO_SEA_PL")
```

```{r}
hexagons <- st_read(dsn = "data/chap17/geospatial", layer = "hexagons")
```

```{r}
eldercare <- st_read(dsn = "data/chap17/geospatial", layer = "ELDERCARE")
```

```{r}
ODMatrix <- read_csv("data/chap17/aspatial/OD_Matrix.csv", skip = 0)
```

## Prepare the data

All three layers are put in the same projected CRS (SVY21, EPSG 3414).

```{r}
mpsz <- st_transform(mpsz, 3414)
eldercare <- st_transform(eldercare, 3414)
hexagons <- st_transform(hexagons, 3414)
```

Each eldercare centre gets a capacity of 100. Each hexagon gets a demand of 100.

```{r}
eldercare <- eldercare %>%
  select(fid, ADDRESSPOS) %>%
  mutate(capacity = 100)
```

```{r}
hexagons <- hexagons %>%
  select(fid) %>%
  mutate(demand = 100)
```

The OD matrix is turned into a wide matrix. Rows are hexagons and columns are eldercare centres. The distance is changed from metres to kilometres.

```{r}
distmat <- ODMatrix %>%
  select(origin_id, destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  spread(destination_id, total_cost) %>%
  select(-origin_id)

distmat_km <- as.matrix(distmat / 1000)
dim(distmat_km)
```

## Compute 2SFCA with catchment_ratio()

`max_cost = 5` sets a 5 km catchment.

```{r}
df_2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  max_cost = 5) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("2SFCA" = ".")
```

```{r}
summary(df_2sfca)
```

About 1,281 hexagons get 0, because no eldercare centre is within 5 km of them.

## Enhanced 2-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA)

```{r}
step_weights <- list(c(5, .01), c(4, .05), c(3, .1), c(2, .4), c(1, 1))
df_e2sfca <- catchment_ratio(
  consumers = hexagons$demand,
  providers = eldercare$capacity,
  cost = distmat_km,
  weight = step_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename("E2SFCA" = ".")
```

```{r}
summary(df_e2sfca)
```

## Compare 2SFCA and E2SFCA

```{r}
hexagon_acc <- bind_cols(hexagons, df_2sfca, df_e2sfca)
head(hexagon_acc)
```

```{r}
cor(hexagon_acc$`2SFCA`, hexagon_acc$E2SFCA, method = "spearman")
```

Both methods have the same mean, because the total capacity is shared out in both cases. E2SFCA has a lower median and a smaller maximum, because centres that are 3 to 5 km away now add very little.
